question: Does the P4BR Thomas clustered spectrum improve over a one-Gaussian spectrum when both are fit only to the existing CC0 colour uniform-scan cohort and then evaluated without refitting on the independent CC0 B&W uniform-scan cohort?

development.unit: one scan after median aggregation across four fixed crops and three RGB channels
development.target: median of eight scan-level normalized log-radial NPS signatures

confirmation.unit: one scan after median aggregation across nine fixed crops

models.fit_space: normalized centered log radial band power
models.acf: unit-zero-lag inverse discrete Fourier transform of the fitted radial spectrum on a 512x512 frequency grid

optimizer.algorithm: deterministic scipy differential_evolution in log10 parameter space then polish

branch_rule.pass: Retain one generic same-scanner clustered-spectrum mechanism candidate and open a separately frozen canonical field/runtime approximation; no stock or microscopic parameter claim.
branch_rule.fail: Close transfer of the exact P4BR one-level Thomas mechanism to these real uniform scans; do not tune on either historical spectra or the same scanner cohorts.

forbidden: fit or inspect B&W confirmation pixels before both models are frozen
treat crops or RGB channels as independent samples
fit stock-specific profiles or infer microscopic particle sizes
change bands, lags, crop locations, parameter bounds, controls or gates after scoring
claim scanner-independent emulsion structure, calibration or product readiness
claim_ceiling: Retrospective mechanism comparison on exact same-scanner CC0 uniform scans with a disjoint colour-fit/B&W-confirmation split; effective scanner-convolved correlation scales only, not stock, process, density, microscopic or product calibration.
